content_groups.group_title: Q: Why do you examine the axilla?

blocks.text: To assess regional lymph nodes, particularly because breast malignancy can spread to the axillary nodes.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What are the concerning features of a breast lump?

blocks.text: A hard, irregular or fixed mass, especially with skin tethering, nipple changes, pathological discharge or lymphadenopathy.
An orange-peel appearance of the breast skin caused by oedema associated with lymphatic obstruction.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What is the significance of a new inverted nipple?

blocks.text: It can be a sign of underlying breast pathology, including malignancy, and requires assessment.

content_groups.group_title: Q: What is Paget disease of the breast?

blocks.text: A form of breast cancer involving the nipple-areolar complex, classically presenting with persistent eczematous or crusting changes of the nipple.
